key_insight: SSB (Self-Supervised Semantic Bridge) enables high-fidelity unpaired image-to-image translation by learning a domain-agnostic semantic latent space that bridges source and target domains, avoiding reliance on target-domain adversarial losses or imperfect diffusion inversions.
problem_solved: Addresses poor generalization of adversarial methods and low-fidelity outputs from diffusion-inversion by providing a self-supervised semantic mapping that enables robust, high-quality translations between unpaired domains.
method: Learn a shared semantic latent space via self-supervised objectives so content is preserved while style/appearance can be changed across domains.

Use an encoder-to-bridge-to-decoder pipeline that conditions a diffusion generator (or decoder) on semantic latents, removing the need for target-domain adversarial training and reducing inversion error.
Integrate contrastive/consistency losses and cross-domain reconstruction to disentangle semantics from domain-specific appearance and stabilize translation.
impact: Enables practitioners to perform unpaired translations with better fidelity and stronger generalization to unseen data, reducing the need for adversarial target-domain supervision and improving reliability of diffusion-based generative pipelines.
visual_elements: Schematic of the semantic bridge: encoder (source) → shared semantic latent → decoder/diffusion (target), with loss icons for self-supervision and consistency.

paper_title: Unpaired Image-to-Image Translation via a Self-Supervised Semantic Bridge
paper_authors: Jiaming Liu, Felix Petersen, Yunhe Gao, Yabin Zhang, Hyojin Kim
